 Follow us on Facebook Twitter Hello Latest news Without a fix, Social Security benefits are facing a cut in six years. The Senator from Vermont has a plan that would increase benefits at the same time.
 Jose Luis Gonzalez Social Security How Bernie Sanders plans to increase Social Security payments by $2,400
 Greg Heilman Update: Nov 11th, 2026 06:44 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google The 2026 Midterm Elections handed Democrats a solid majority in the House and Senate shifting power away from the Republicans for the next two years. Their candidates ran on issues of affordability and protecting entitlement programs like Social Security, and the American public will be looking to them to fulfil their promises.
 On the issue of Social Security, lawmakers have a limited amount of time to fix the funding shortfall to the program before the trust fund that supports retirement benefits runs out of money. When that happens, under law the Social Security Administration will have to cut benefits by at least 22% .
 Sanders’ “top priority will be to expand Social Security benefits by at least $2,400”
 The Independent Senator from Vermont, Bernie Sanders , posted on social media that not only does he have a plan to close the funding gap and shore up the program’s financing well into the future but that it will boost benefits.
 “As the next chair of the Social Security Subcommittee, a top priority will be to expand Social Security benefits by at least $2,400 a year & extend Social Security’s solvency for generations,” he wrote. “How? By scrapping the cap & demanding that the wealthy pay their fair share of taxes.” 
 This measure for securing that the Social Security program has enough revenue to cover its outlays as well as the ability to fortify the trust fund for future retirees is popular among the American public . Democrats have been calling for this for several years now, and it has also been gaining traction among some Republicans .
 Expand Social Security Now! pic.twitter.com/6O3Ry0y8E5 
— Social Security Works (@SSWorks) November 9, 2026 
 Currently in 2026, Americans only have to pay Social Security taxes on income up to $184,500. That amount will increase to $192,300 next year.
